findings.reason: the section must name the coverage predicate as the gate's one owner of the question and state how the findings record is chosen from its result, or the gate keeps two coverage readers that drift as the key changes.
findings.text: the gate still selects one record by whole-document fingerprint (`read_plan_review`, then `_store_delivered_plan_review` at :2598 which itself calls `read_plan_review` at :2605) while §16's coverage predicate answers a different question over the union of section digests across every stored review; §16 says the predicate is "called from the same place … that calls that step today" but never says the gate now answers by the predicate alone, nor which single record's `unanswered_findings` it checks when coverage comes from a union of several stored reviews, so the two answers can disagree

findings.text: the Interface accounting paragraph cites "the 1478 that §18 left" and "grows by three over the 1478", but the count handed to this review is public_definitions 1480, and §17 has already landed its heading reader and machinery-element predicate (its own record: 1478→1480), so §16's remaining addition is one over 1480, not three over 1478; the section substitutes a count from an earlier revision for the current week's figure

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the whole design hides its complexity behind one existing name, `plan_fingerprint`, plus one private helper (`_section_digests`) and one private coverage predicate; there is no spread of same-level wrappers over the section-digest machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 leaves `require_plan_reviewed` answering "is this plan covered" two ways: the existing whole-document `read_plan_review`/`_store_delivered_plan_review` join at `reckon/crew/routing.py:2666` and `:2598`, beside the new section-set coverage predicate it adds "from the same place".
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — the supplied week reads public_definitions 1480, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 accounts for its one addition against 1478, a superseded count, and treats §17's two additions as future.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — both open sections name the existing machinery they extend: §16 reuses `reckon/_plan_html.py`'s `_TAG_RE` (line 1804), the §17 raw-text span reader (`plan_headings`, `structured_section_spans`), `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`, `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates`, `landed_section_ids`, and `roadmap.implementable_sections`; §19 reuses the exported `SECTION_NUMBER_PATTERN` core and `followup_pointers._INVOCATION_RE`, and adds no subsystem without a cited mechanism.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 states in its own text why the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (single-record-to-one-digest join versus a set-to-union join) and why `strip_tags` is not a second tag expression (`count_open_decisions` keeps its bare `_TAG_RE.sub` because the richer stripper would flip the open-decision count).
